content.title: Arrays: Work With Ordered Values
content.hook: Sometimes the program needs more than one related value. An array stores values in an ordered list.
content.context: Sometimes the program needs more than one related value. An array stores values in an ordered list.
goals: Create arrays, access items by index, and use simple iteration over ordered collections.

content.title: Create an array
content.text:
```js
const colors = ["red", "blue", "green"];
```

The values have positions called indexes. JavaScript starts counting from `0` here, so:

- index `0` → `"red"`
- index `1` → `"blue"`
- index `2` → `"green"`

activities.title: Change one access
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
What is `colors[2]`?


The index selects a position; it does not mean "give me the second value" in a human-counting sense. The first position is index `0`.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.

feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.title: Iterate
Build
content.text:
Create an array named `tools` containing three strings: `"HTML"`, `"CSS"`, and `"JavaScript"`.

One valid answer:

```js
const tools = ["HTML", "CSS", "JavaScript"];
```

takeaways: **Mental model:** An array is an ordered collection.
**Senior habit:** When reasoning about an array, write down the positions and values before changing the loop that uses them.
